claim_verdicts.evidence: Key shell fits, but the claim quotes older manual wording. Bash 5.3 manual 3.4.2 now reads: '($?) Expands to the exit status of the most recently executed command.' Pipeline status is in 3.2.3: 'the exit status of the last command in the pipeline, unless the pipefail option is enabled'. The idea (a chain judged as one, replaced by the next command) holds; prior execution r2 `echo; echo q:$?; false; echo q:$?` -> q:0, q:1. Body wording ('one command, or a chain judged as one') needs no change.
claim_verdicts.source: gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html (Edition 5.3), 3.4.2 Special Parameters, 3.2.3 Pipelines; execution r2
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: `$?` expands to the exit status of the most recently executed command; a chain built with `|` counts as one command (a pipeline) whose status is its last command's, or with pipefail the last one to fail, so `$?` reports on that one thing only, and the next command replaces it.
